findings.summary: The limits list names "a diff driver, textconv or `log.showSignature` the local config names" as the ways config makes git start a program. Two config routes that reach the %G check this round closes are not named. A `pretty.<name>` alias holding `%GG` is used through `--format=<name>`, a word with no `%G` in it. A `format.pretty` default holding `%GG` applies to a bare `git log`/`git show`. Both start gpg or ssh-keygen and pass the regex at review-panel.js:155, because the list only checks the command line. The general premise ("git reads its own config") covers them, but after round 2 corrected overstated claims, the named examples read as exhaustive. Add these two routes, or say the examples are not complete.

summary: Round 3 replaces `a.includes('%G')` with `new RegExp('%[-+ ]?G')` (review-panel.js:34, :155). The new pattern matches everything the old one did, so the check is stricter, not looser. It covers each modifier git reads between `%` and the placeholder letter (`+`, `-`, space). git reads only one modifier, and `%<(N)` or `%>(N)` prefixes still leave a `%G` substring, so no form of the signature placeholder gets through on the command line. Five new refusal cases cover all three modifiers, including a space inside quotes and a `tformat:` form. Refusing a literal `%%G` is a false positive, which is the safe direction. The install test gets a fourth input (one key on one line, a second key over two lines), with no change to install.sh. The guard.json hash moves to `32cc9711…`, and the DECISIONS.md text matches it. No check is weakened or removed, and the diff contains no secrets. One minor point: the limit recorded in DECISIONS.md does not name a config route that reaches the same signature check.
